sentences.text: The genus name Dearcmhara means "marine lizard" in Scottish Gaelic, marking one of the few times a fossil has received a Gaelic name.
Dearcmhara is classified as a basal neoichthyosaurian ichthyosaur.
The type species was discovered in 1959 by fossil hunter Brian Shawcross in Bearreraig Bay on the Trotternish peninsula of Skye.
It was not until 2014 that a scientific project identified the fossils as belonging to a previously unknown species.
The discovery was announced on 11 January 2015 in a study published in the Scottish Journal of Geology.
Dearcmhara lived from the Toarcian to the Bajocian stages, between 184.2 and 168.6 million years ago.
